label: early "p" input (strongest at sequence start); weaker on 1 / <DEL> after particular prefixes
explanation: Low-end candidate unit almost entirely in the original-input and delimiter phases (82% of mass original, 17.5% delimiter, ~0.5% copy). Its clearest trigger is the input token p: p at t=0 fires every time (dev precision 1.0), and p at t=1 fires about 58% of the time. Input p accounts for ~53% of activation mass, input 1 for ~22% and <DEL> for ~17.5%, with small contributions from k and b. Firing on p/1 later in the sequence, and on <DEL>, is strongly context dependent: it is mostly limited to t<=4, happens more in short sequences (L=3-4), and depends on which tokens came earlier (prefixes from a, l, w, d, n, o raise it; others such as e, v, x, i suppress it), in a way no simple prefix-set predicate captured. The largest activations are on <DEL> after short prefixes like "a l k", "o w k" or "l w k", and on p or 1 at t=2-3 after prefixes like "a d" or "a w 2". It almost never fires on repeated tokens (in_first=0 carries 8% of mass) or during the copy phase. The predicate p-at-t<=1 has high precision but covers only about 40% of the mass.
